focus: Democrats win House and Senate: Dow futures +912 (+1.75%), IWM +1.6%, QQQ only +0.2%
Texas governor flips on a data center moratorium pledge: CRWV -7.8%, VRT -6.9%, ORCL -4.5%
Datadog -17.8% on beat-and-raise with an in-line Q4 sales guide; SNOW -5%, PLTR -5%
AMD beat (adj. EPS $2.09 vs $1.95) but trades -0.7%; ANET +6% on a big Q4 guide
Health care leads (XLV +2.4%): Molina +6%, Centene +5%, Novo +5.4% on a raised outlook
Yields and oil ease: 10-yr ~4.92% (-3 bp), WTI 94.17 (-2%); ARM, QCOM report tonight
bigPicture: The market reads the blue wave as gridlock and less deficit spending: yields dip, the dollar falls (-0.6%), and money goes to small caps, banks, health insurers and staples rather than to tech.

The AI trade has a new risk on top of the capex-peak worry: state limits on data centers. Texas holds roughly 27-30% of planned U.S. capacity, so neoclouds, power gear and Oracle sell while hyperscalers are mostly higher.
Good numbers are not enough for richly valued software and chips: Datadog beat and raised and fell 18%; AMD beat and is flat. Only guidance surprises get paid (Arista).
Rates still set the ceiling: a December 9 hike remains the base case (~75-85% per the Movers Report), with Hammack Thursday and jobs and Musalem Friday.
snapshot.takeaway: The index gap is a rotation, not a broad risk-on day: Dow and small caps up, AI infrastructure and software down on a new policy risk. Let the first 15 minutes show whether the AI gap-downs (TSLA, CRWV, VRT) fill or extend before trusting either side; Arm and Qualcomm report tonight.

sectors.text: Texas Gov.-elect Hinojosa pledged to halt new data center approvals; Bloomberg says Democratic wins could affect nearly half of proposed U.S. AI capacity. Oracle also cancelled a $7B Tencent chip-leasing deal. CRWV -7.8%, ORCL -4.5%; MSFT +2.1%, GOOGL +0.7%.
Arista guided Q4 to $3.9-4.0B vs $3.60B and is +6%; Super Micro's fiscal 2027 sales guide topped estimates (+1.2%). Power and cooling sell on the Texas risk: VRT -6.9%, ETN -4.3%.
AMD beat and guided above consensus yet trades -0.7%; Skyworks -11% on a weak guide; MU -2.3%, SKHY -2%, SMH -1.3%. Arm, Qualcomm and Coherent report after the close.
Datadog -17.8% despite raising its full-year guide, because Q4 revenue was guided only in line; SNOW -5.0%, PLTR -5.1%, MDB -4.4%. CRM +2.5% and MSFT +2.1% buck it.
WTI 94.17 (-2.0%), Brent 101.58 (-2.0%); Iran's speaker welcomed the vote as 'NO TO WAR' while Khamenei ordered forces to answer any threat. XLE -0.2%, MPC -2.8%.
XLV +2.4% premarket; insurers rally on the Democratic win (Molina +6.3%, Centene ~+5%), Novo +5.4% on a raised 2026 outlook, CVS -2.4% on its plan to split in two.
